title: Sedation assessment

sources.use: PADIS 2018 and 2025 focused update: recommendation statements; licence RED/unverified
Official 2025 recommendation statements on sedation and anxiety; full paper not appraised.

objectives: Assess pain and sedation with validated tools at the ordered frequency.
Record the target and actual score and report persistent deviation.
Take part in daily awakening trials safely when ordered.

items.text: Perform the daily sedation interruption or spontaneous awakening trial when ordered and the patient is suitable, with team safety checks; watch for agitation, distress, desaturation or haemodynamic change and follow the protocol for stopping or restarting.

The SCCM 2025 focused update conditionally favours dexmedetomidine rather than propofol in mechanically ventilated adults when lighter sedation or delirium reduction is a leading priority. This is not a universal sedative preference; patient-specific goals, contraindications and the prescriber's plan govern.
Assess at the ordered frequency with validated tools; record the target and actual score; report persistent deviation; reassess after every dose change and procedure.
Where a protocol allows, titrate sedatives to the prescribed target score (nurse-protocolised targeted sedation).
Titration authority is set by order or protocol; doses are not given in this library.
Scale level definitions (RASS, SAS) are not reproduced; use the unit-approved tool and its training.

A sedation score describes observable arousal or agitation but does not by itself diagnose delirium. When altered behaviour is new, also assess oxygenation, pain, neurological change and other plausible causes, and escalate any acute deterioration rather than automatically adjusting the sedative.

During neuromuscular blockade, movement-based sedation scales cannot establish consciousness or comfort. Verify the prescribed analgesia and sedation plan and seek team-directed monitoring of sedation depth; processed EEG may assist in selected deeply sedated or paralysed patients. Absence of movement alone does not establish adequate sedation.

When a patient appears anxious, assess distress, communication needs, pain, breathing and possible acute deterioration before attributing the presentation to anxiety. The 2025 SCCM update found inadequate evidence to make a recommendation on benzodiazepines specifically for anxiety in adult ICU patients. Do not treat anxiety as an automatic indication for a sedative; discuss individualized management with the responsible team.
Record scores, target and trend; reassess after any change.

When the patient is too deeply sedated or otherwise unable to undergo the unit-approved delirium tool, document that the screen could not be completed and why, then reassess eligibility under the unit's validated tool instructions; do not record a reassuring negative result.
Report persistent deviation from target, agitation or over-sedation.

For unexpectedly reduced responsiveness, marked new agitation or an unsafe deviation from target, assess airway, breathing, circulation, pain and prescribed medication delivery and obtain urgent clinician review. Changes in sedation are not a substitute for identifying causes of deterioration.
Record tool, score, target, interventions and response per your unit's documentation standard.

checklist.text: Use the unit's validated tool and record target and actual score.
Assess pain as well as sedation.
Titrate only within the order or protocol.
Reassess after every dose change and procedure.
Assess new reduced responsiveness or unsafe agitation immediately, including airway, breathing and circulation; escalate urgently rather than waiting for persistent deviation.
Document delirium screening separately from sedation/arousal scoring; if not assessable, record the reason rather than a false negative result.

During neuromuscular blockade, movement-based sedation scales cannot establish consciousness or comfort. Verify the prescribed analgesia and sedation plan and seek team-directed monitoring of sedation depth; processed EEG may assist in selected deeply sedated or paralysed patients. Absence of movement alone does not establish adequate sedation.

When a patient appears anxious, assess distress, communication needs, pain, breathing and possible acute deterioration before attributing the presentation to anxiety. The 2025 SCCM update found inadequate evidence to make a recommendation on benzodiazepines specifically for anxiety in adult ICU patients. Do not treat anxiety as an automatic indication for a sedative; discuss individualized management with the responsible team.

gaps: RASS/SAS definitions, dosing and neuromuscular blockade procedures are not covered. Selected PADIS guidance on depth monitoring during paralysis is mapped; device-specific interpretation and specialist oversight remain necessary.
PADIS full text: recommendation statements only.

SCCM 2025 recommendation-level statements support an ICU-wide multifactorial response, but this lesson does not contain licensed CAM-ICU or ICDSC scoring instructions or independent patient-specific sedation orders.
